rows.used_for: P1A/P1B blackboard control structure (partitioned panels, KS triggering, agenda scheduler; BB1 control blackboard and version tags)
rows.citation: Hayes-Roth, Barbara (1985). A blackboard architecture for control. Artificial Intelligence 26(3), 251-321. doi:10.1016/0004-3702(85)90063-9
rows.relation: faithful adaptation (panels + KSAR agenda + append-only hypothesis history; BB1-style world-version control fact for P1B)
simplifications: KS ratings collapsed to a fixed priority ladder (answer > expand) instead of learned ratings
no opportunistic scheduling heuristics; the agenda is drained to quiescence
hypothesis indexing reduced to a tail posting index (BB1 had general hypothesis indexing)

rows.used_for: blackboard precedent line (Hearsay-II panels and KSAR terminology)
rows.citation: Erman, L.D., Hayes-Roth, F., Lesser, V.R., Reddy, D.R. (1980). The Hearsay-II speech-understanding system: Integrating knowledge to resolve uncertainty. ACM Computing Surveys 12(2), 213-253.
rows.relation: terminology and panel structure only; no speech-specific content
simplifications: no acoustic-phonetic levels; two-level generic field/closure panels

rows.used_for: P2 Soar working memory (WMEs, goal scoping, i-support retraction, input-link perception)
rows.citation: Soar Manual, section 4: Procedural Knowledge & Learning. University of Michigan.
rows.relation: faithful adaptation at the working-memory level
simplifications: operator preference resolution and impasses are NOT exercised: the closure is elaboration-level, resolved by support-retraction to quiescence
input-link perception fires at stream update events only (not per decision cycle)

rows.used_for: P3/P3R ACT-R module buffers (strict capacity, declarative memory, retrieval requests, buffer swaps)
rows.citation: Anderson, J.R., Bothell, D., Byrne, M.D., Douglass, S., Lebiere, C., Qin, Y. (2004). An integrated theory of the mind. Psychological Review 111(4), 1036-1050.
rows.relation: faithful adaptation of the buffer/DM core
simplifications: base-level activation approximated by deterministic most-recently-accessed selection
no subsymbolic utilities, no production compilation

rows.used_for: P0 incumbent working state (structural adjacency index, per-query liveness, ATMS-style revocation propagation semantics)
rows.citation: de Kleer, J. (1986). An assumption-based truth maintenance system. Artificial Intelligence 28(2), 127-224.
rows.relation: the incumbent mechanism this study measures against (pre-existing on main)

rows.used_for: revocation/retraction semantics context (TMS lineage of the sweep phase)
rows.citation: Doyle, J. (1979). A truth maintenance system. Artificial Intelligence 12(3), 231-272.
rows.relation: lineage note only; not implemented as an arm

rows.used_for: update-locality reference definition (impact cone as least dependency-closed superset; self-adjusting computation context)
rows.citation: Acar, U.A. (2005). Self-Adjusting Computation. PhD thesis, Carnegie Mellon University, CMU-CS-05-129.
rows.relation: conceptual reference for change propagation costing; the cone itself is production code (src/ocm/kso/revocation.py impact_cone)

rows.used_for: drift arm rationale (retraction on mismatch between working state and world)
rows.citation: VanLehn, K. (1988). Toward a theory of impasse-driven learning. In: Foundation of Knowledge Acquisition, Machine Learning 8. Springer.
rows.relation: motivates the mid-stream catalogue drift as an impasse source

rows.used_for: donor reference (the neural residual-stream analogue this lane maps working state onto)
rows.citation: Vaswani, A., et al. (2017). Attention Is All You Need. NeurIPS 30.
rows.relation: analogy anchor only; no transformer component is built or claimed replaced

in_repo_sources.use: gated_closure: oracle and incumbent mirror semantics
incumbent index semantics mirrored (snapshot-bound, charged rebuild)

notes: no claim is made that the blackboard architecture is novel
no AGI / LLM_EQUIVALENT / TRANSFORMER_REPLACED / GENERAL_SUPERIORITY claim is made anywhere in this capsule
every simplification above is a declared reduction of the parent, not an enhancement claimed as the parent's
